usageNotes: Use this endpoint to start a stopped or paused LXC container on a remote PVE node managed by Proxmox Datacenter Manager. The caller must hold the Resource.Manage privilege on the remote/guest path. The operation is asynchronous — the response is a remote UPID string; poll the corresponding task endpoint to confirm the container reaches running state before depending on it.

examples.summary: Start LXC container 201 on remote 'hetzner-de' (let PDM pick the node)

tips: If the target LXC is on a specific node in the remote cluster, pass 'node' to avoid ambiguity — otherwise PDM resolves the node automatically.
The returned UPID is scoped to the remote; use the remote task-status endpoint (not the local PVE one) to track completion.
Starting a container that is already running returns an error — check container status first if your workflow may call this redundantly.
